newsitem.title: USA: GTE to buy BBN and fiber optic network; sets Cisco alliance.
newsitem.headline: GTE to buy BBN and fiber optic network; sets Cisco alliance.

text.p: GTE Corp. said Tuesday it will buy Internet service provider BBN Corp. for $616 million as part of a major initiative to make itself into a leading national provider of integrated telecommunications services.

GTE also said it entered a strategic alliance with Cisco Systems Inc. to develop enhanced data and internet services and said it would buy a national, state-of-the-art fiber-optic network from Qwest Communications.
The company, based in Stamford, Conn., said it would pay $29 a share for BBN -- a 28 percent premium over the stock's $22.625 closing price Monday.
The moves are aimed at positioning GTE as a "market-leading national provider of integrated telecommunications services," it said in a statement.
GTE, one of the largest publicly held telecommunications companies in the world, already offers local and wireless service in 29 states and long-distance service in all 50 states.
Under the terms of the BBN acquisition, which has been approved by the boards of both companies, GTE will start a cash tender offer for BBN "shortly."

Cambridge, Mass.-based BBN provides high-performance, end-to-end Internet solutions such as World Wide Web site hosting, network security, consulting, systems integration and dedicated and dial-up Internet access for government and commercial customers.
GTE said the BBN acquisition will "jump-start" its chances of winning contracts to provide enhanced Internet services for large businesses.
It added that its pact with networking powerhouse Cisco will enable GTE to deliver bundled solutions of applications, equipment installation, maintenance and telecommunication services.
In a statement released jointly with Cisco, GTE said its purchases of Cisco products for resale could reach over $1 billion.

All the moves are aimed at making GTE a "national 'one-stop' provider of local, long-distance, Internet and wireless services, and will establish an advanced data network that will be fully operational next year," GTE President Kent Foster said in a statement.
"At that point, we will be in a position to reach virtually the entire U.S. population," Foster added.

GTE said that through its acquisition of 24 "dark" fibers in privately held Qwest Communications' national network it will have a fiber optic network that stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific by 1998.
"GTE's network will greatly reduce the high up-front cost of today's private data networks, making advanced data communications more affordable for a greater segment of the populations," it said.
